I have farmed here a long time, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked on my land before, then I change a little if I think the money can come back. On 6 mu, I cannot spend wildly, but I also will not save fertilizer and then watch the yield fall. Cotton is still my main crop, so I will put the best land and more fertilizer there. Wheat and maize I will keep, but a bit tighter on cost. I have well water, so I am less afraid of dry spells than people who wait for rain. Around here, when people see cotton can still make money, they usually feed it a bit heavier, especially nitrogen and potash, because if cotton grows weak later, it is hard to pull it back. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer, and give winter water and spring water if needed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is common now and the stand is better. I have middle school education, so I do look at balance, not only habit: wheat needs steady fertilizer and water, maize needs quick strength in summer, and cotton needs longer feeding through the season. Labor in my family is not all available because some work off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple: rotary tillage where it saves effort, a few solid irrigations, and pesticide sprays timed to real pressure, not too few.
